title: Vow and Songbook
premise: August Dravenmoor has spent a decade ghostwriting other people's truths while burying his own — including the sentence he rehearsed for ten years and never said to the one who left. When his estranged family demands he bring a partner to the reunion that will decide who inherits Dravenmoor House, he hires Wren Solano, a session musician who owes him a favor and hides debts of her own. What begins as a transactional performance turns devastatingly real, until August discovers Wren is secretly the anonymous memoirist whose manuscript about her own family's survival is the very book he's been hired to erase for a rival publisher. To keep her story alive and claim the inheritance on their own terms, they must each say the truest sentence they know — hers in print, his out loud — before the estate, and their chance at love, is signed away.
about_author: Wendell Zhou is the pen name of a former wedding pianist turned novelist who writes love stories set against family obligations and old houses with too many secrets. They live quietly with a rescue greyhound and an unfinished songbook they swear will stay unfinished.

chapters.title: The Ghost in the Margins
chapters.summary: August's POV. He finishes ghosting a celebrity memoir, deleting every trace of himself from another person's truth. Introduces his rule: love stays in past tense. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as professionalism.

chapters.title: A Favor Owed
chapters.summary: August's POV. A letter arrives: the Dravenmoor reunion, inheritance vote, plus-one required. He tracks down Wren Solano, who once played his sister's funeral and still owes him for covering her studio debt. Beat: reluctant bargain struck.

chapters.title: Terms of Engagement
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She agrees to be his fake date for one weekend, hiding that she's behind an anonymous memoir manuscript her agent calls unsellable. Beat: guarded attraction masked as negotiation.

chapters.title: The House That Remembers
chapters.summary: August's POV. They arrive at Dravenmoor House; his mother greets Wren like an audition, his brother like a threat. Beat: August realizes bringing Wren home reopens wounds he'd bricked over.

chapters.title: Duet for One Weekend
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Pressed to perform after dinner, she plays; August joins her unprompted on an old family piano. The room goes quiet. Beat: first crack in the fake-dating armor.

chapters.title: Brother's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: August's POV. Brother Julian corners him: the inheritance hinges on proving stability, and Julian suspects the relationship is staged. Beat: stakes sharpen — this lie now has witnesses.

chapters.title: The Anonymous Author
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Back home, Wren learns the rival publisher — August's current client — wants to buy and bury a memoir about a family that survived by betrayal. It's hers. Beat: dread; her two worlds are converging.

chapters.title: Second Date, First Truth
chapters.summary: August's POV. To sell the romance to suspicious relatives, they stage dates in public. Over dessert, Wren asks what he never told anyone about his sister. He answers. Beat: intimacy arrives uninvited.

chapters.title: Rehearsed Sentence
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. She finds a decade-old letter draft in August's coat — the sentence he rehearsed and never sent. She doesn't ask. Beat: tenderness tangled with trespass.

chapters.title: The Rival's Offer
chapters.summary: August's POV. His client offers a fortune to ghost a takedown of the anonymous memoirist, whom the client has identified as 'a musician.' August accepts to protect Wren without telling her. Beat: loyalty curdling into deception.

chapters.title: Family Portrait, Cracked Frame
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Second reunion weekend: Julian stages a photo op; August's mother privately offers Wren money to leave. Wren refuses — not for August, but on principle. Beat: Wren stops being a hireling.

chapters.title: What Survival Cost
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Flashback chapter: how Wren's family survived bankruptcy by betraying her father's partner, and why she wrote the memoir anonymously. Beat: the price of survival made concrete.

chapters.title: The Erasure Contract
chapters.summary: August's POV. He drafts the takedown memoir, recognizing Wren's voice in the source material line by line. He stalls, rewriting instead of destroying. Beat: guilt becomes unbearable.

chapters.title: Rain on the Conservatory
chapters.summary: Both POVs alternating. Trapped by a storm, they stop performing. Almost-kiss interrupted by Julian. Beat: desire acknowledged but deferred.

chapters.title: Julian's Ledger
chapters.summary: August's POV. August discovers Julian has been embezzling from the estate to cover gambling debts — the real reason Julian needs the inheritance. Beat: moral inversion; the villain has reasons.

chapters.title: Manuscript in the Mail
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Her agent sells the memoir — to August's client, who plans to publish it gutted, credited to a ghostwriter. Wren realizes someone inside knows her identity. Beat: trap closing.

chapters.title: The Rehearsal Dinner Lie
chapters.summary: August's POV. At a family dinner, August publicly claims a future with Wren — engagement implied — to block Julian's maneuver. Wren plays along, then confronts him privately. Beat: the fake escalates beyond contract.

chapters.title: Past Tense, Present Danger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers August is the ghostwriter assigned to erase her book. She says nothing, gathering evidence. Beat: heartbreak weaponized into strategy.

chapters.title: The Mother's Terms
chapters.summary: August's POV. His mother reveals the reunion vote was engineered to force August home; she wanted him to reclaim the house, not inherit it conditionally. Beat: inheritance reframed as cage.

chapters.title: Interlude: Songbook Pages
chapters.summary: Dual POV, epistolary. Alternating entries from August's unsent letters and Wren's memoir drafts, mirroring each other across years. Beat: quiet devastation; two people writing truths they can't speak.

chapters.title: Caught Between Covers
chapters.summary: Julian's POV (single deviation). Julian finds Wren's original manuscript and recognizes the betrayal it documents — it implicates a business partner connected to the Dravenmoors. Beat: leverage discovered.

chapters.title: Blackmail in B Minor
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Julian blackmails Wren: withdraw from August's life or he publishes her identity and buries the memoir anyway. Beat: loyalty vs. truth forced into open conflict.

chapters.title: The Withdrawal
chapters.summary: August's POV. Wren abruptly ends the arrangement, citing the contract's completion clause. August, wounded, signs the erasure deal in a act of self-punishment. Beat: lowest point approaching.

chapters.title: Empty Stage
chapters.summary: August's POV. Alone in Dravenmoor House, August rereads the takedown draft and finally admits he's been ghosting his own life. He burns nothing yet decides everything. Beat: turning inward.

chapters.title: The Agent's Confession
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren's agent confesses she sold Wren out to Julian months ago. Wren realizes the whole sale was orchestrated. Beat: rage converted to resolve.

chapters.title: Counterpoint
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren registers the memoir under her own name with a new publisher and prepares to go public — knowing it may destroy the Dravenmoor vote and August's standing. Beat: choosing truth over safety.

chapters.title: The Vote
chapters.summary: August's POV. Reunion climax begins: the inheritance vote. Julian presents evidence of August's 'fake' relationship. August, instead of denying it, tells the room the truth — including that he paid Wren. Beat: public ruin chosen over comfortable lie.

chapters.title: Sentence, Spoken
chapters.summary: August's POV. Before the stunned family, August finally says the rehearsed sentence — not to Wren, but aloud as testimony: what he should have said ten years ago at his sister's bedside, and what he means now. Beat: catharsis; the decade-long debt paid.

chapters.title: Wren's Testimony
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren enters mid-chaos and reads the opening chapter of her memoir to the assembled family — naming the betrayal that entwines both families. Beat: truth as inheritance.

chapters.title: Julian Unbound
chapters.summary: August's POV. Confronted with exposure, Julian confesses the embezzlement rather than let Wren's book do it for him. The vote collapses; the house passes to no one cleanly. Beat: justice without triumph.

chapters.title: What the House Keeps
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. In the aftermath, August's mother, stripped of her scheme, gives Wren her sister-in-law's old songbook — the one August's late sister started. Beat: grief shared becomes inheritance of a better kind.

chapters.title: Erasure Undone
chapters.summary: August's POV. August terminates the ghostwriting contract, forfeiting his fee and reputation in publishing circles, and hands Wren every copy of the takedown draft. Beat: price of survival paid willingly.

chapters.title: The Long Silence After
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Weeks later, Wren hesitates to call August — the memoir's publication looms, and she fears being his next ghostwritten chapter. Beat: fear of repeating old patterns.

chapters.title: Byline
chapters.summary: August's POV. August buys the first copy of Wren's published memoir, her name on the cover, and writes her a letter that is entirely, clumsily his own voice. Beat: vulnerability without performance.

chapters.title: Encore, Unscheduled
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren shows up at August's apartment with the sister's songbook and sets terms: no ghosts, no contracts, past tense abolished. Beat: reconciliation on equal footing.

chapters.title: Dravenmoor, Repurposed
chapters.summary: August's POV. The family converts the house into a residency for writers and musicians; August declines ownership, takes a room instead. Beat: inheritance redefined as stewardship.

chapters.title: First Draft of Forever
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. First real date — no audience, no payment. They write together at the same table, occasionally reading aloud. Beat: ordinary joy earned.

chapters.title: The Song They Finished
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At the house's opening concert, they complete the sister's unfinished song, August singing the line he once could only write. Beat: full-circle musical resolution.

chapters.title: Vow
chapters.summary: August's POV. Not a wedding — a vow exchange in the conservatory where they almost kissed: promises spoken plainly, witnessed only by the house. Beat: commitment without spectacle.

chapters.title: Coda: Present Tense
chapters.summary: Dual POV, brief alternating paragraphs. One year later: Wren's memoir shortlisted, August publishing under his own name for the first time, the songbook finally finished. Final line returns to the rehearsed sentence — now spoken daily. Beat: peace; love in present tense.
